    🐱 Kludosy¶

    "Our blood remembers the leash. We remember why we cut it."

    Kludosy is the faith of Estran — the western nation of High Catmen (Mediterranean-featured, black-haired, feline humanoids) on Yak Island, below the Mountain Tribe and southwest of the Cubra Tribe. It is a catmen survival faith transposed onto demon soil, built around a single biological fact that determines every law, rite, and taboo: mutable genes.

    High Catmen carry mutable genes that make roughly 90% of offspring with any partner — human, demon, orc, or other catman — present as catmen. The faith treats this not as blessing but as terrifying responsibility.

    Origins¶

    Central Erisdar Persecution¶

    Kludosy did not begin on Yak Island. It began in Central Erisdar, where catmen enclaves — especially the High Catmen ancestors of the Estrani — suffered intensified persecution during the height of the Erisian Church's power (the period of the Erisian Theocracy's consolidation in Ages 7–8). Erisian clerics framed mutable catmen reproduction as "species theft" — that a human woman bearing a catman child was proof of corruption.

    Pogroms, forced separations, and bounty edicts drove many High Catmen to the coasts and thence across the seas. A Mediterranean catmen remnant that fled westward via West Erisdar and the Asatru Knight's Thorn corridor eventually found refuge on the far eastern fringe of the Demon Continent — Yak Island — where the Asatru Empire's laissez-faire "shared demonic nationality" offered protection in exchange for settlement labor.

    Codification on Estran¶

    On arrival, the refugees formalized their survival ethic into Kludosy (from kludo- = "to close, to latch" — the gene that latches catmen form). The first Estrani council, around ~450 AGD, declared three principles: remember the persecution, regulate the mutable blood, and do not become what persecuted you.

    Kludosy's prophet is not a person but an event: The Cutting — the mass decision, made on the beaches of Estran, to cease forced mating and endogamous panic, and instead choose restraint as law rather than have it imposed as chain.

    Beliefs¶

    • 90% catmen offspring — this is not legend but observed heredity. A High Catmen union with any partner produces ~90% phenotypically High Catmen children (black-haired, feline-featured). The remaining ~10% track the partner's lineage. The faith treats this statistic as moral center: with great assimilative power comes great obligation to not assimilate.
    • The taboo against leveraging it — to deliberately use mutable genes to "catten" other populations is Kludosy's gravest sin — called kludo-theft. Arranged unions, seduction campaigns, or demographic pressure to spread catmen form are forbidden and excommunicable.
    • Voluntary restraint as atonement — Estrani are taught to regard persecution and counter-persecution symmetrically: Central Erisdar's fear that catmen would "take" human children was evil, but catmen actually taking would be evil too. The ethical answer is freely chosen restraint.
    • Not Kirivs-bin — Kludosy is a catmen faith, not a demon faith. Estrani respect Kirivs-bin (their demon neighbors' way) and participate in Yak Island's shared festivals, but Kludosy venerates catmen ancestors who endured the Erisian pogroms — not Kirivis. It is sibling to Calism and Sytrenis in spirit, distinct from both in law.
    • Memory is liturgy — to remember Central Erisdar accurately (without exaggeration, without self-pity) is the faith's first practice; distortion in either direction is considered liturgical error.

    Practices¶

    • Taboo register — every Estrani union with a non-catman is recorded in the Kludo Register — not to forbid it (the faith does not forbid exogamy) but to counsel it: the couple meets with a Kludosy elder who explains the 90% likelihood and the obligation not to leverage it.
    • The Leash-Cutting — initiation at adulthood: a youth's childhood cord-bracelet (woven in Central Erisdar style) is cut, signifying that no Erisian leash binds them and no Estrani chain replaces it.
    • Season of Veils — a week each year when all High Catmen wear simple veils over feline features, recalling the years when catmen hid to survive. Demons and other Yak Island neighbors are invited to walk unveiled among them.
    • Gene education — Kludosy temples double as mendelian schools: diagrams, lineage charts, and frank fertility counseling far beyond the medical knowledge of most Erisdar faiths.
    • No clerical celibacy, no endogamy law — Kludosy explicitly forbids laws requiring catmen to marry catmen ("that would be the pogrom inverted"). The faith regulates intention, not pairing.

    Relation to Catmen Faiths & Kirivs-bin¶

    • Kin to Sytrenis and Calism: shares the catmen emphasis on diplomacy, gentleness, and self-greatening, but Kludosy's unique burden (mutable genes + persecution memory) makes it law-heavier than either.
    • Separate from Kirivs-bin: not a sect, not anti-. An Estrani may honor both Kludosy and Kirivs-bin without contradiction; many Yak Island workers attend Demonism night-shift liturgy and Kludosy counsel in the same week.
    • Contrast with Gedarism: where Gedarism defines itself against the bin, Kludosy simply is not the bin — a quieter, more survivable stance for a minority faith on a demon continent.

    Influence¶

    • Majority: Estran — universal among High Catmen on Yak Island; the council of Kludosy elders is consulted on all demographic policy
    • Diaspora: High Catmen trading enclaves in West Erisdar (Zane, Aenid Kingdom ports) and around the Asatru Knight's Thorn maintain Kludosy registers and Leash-Cutting rites; some Central Erisdar High Catmen practice Kludosy covertly despite Erisian pressure
    • Reputation on Yak Island: regarded by diablos and Yak neighbors as exacting but principled — "the cats who count before they leap, nine times over"
    • Central Erisdar wound: the Pontificate has occasionally demanded Estrani registers as "proof of compliance"; Estran's categorical refusal is the island's oldest diplomatic crisis, renewed each decade
